newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS confirms Laidlaw debt at BBB (high).
newsitem.headline: DBRS confirms Laidlaw debt at BBB (high).

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Wednesday it confirmed the rating on the unsecured debentures and notes of Laidlaw Inc at BBB (high), with a stable trend.

DBRS said the confirmation follows Laidlaw's proposed acquisition of American Medical Response Inc, as well as a separate deal involving Rollins Environmental Services Inc and Laidlaw's environmental services business.

DBRS said the takeover of AMR will more than double Laidlaw's existing health care business and create the largest health care transportation company in the United States, with a 14 percent market share. The takeover, which will require the approval of at least two-thirds of AMR's shareholders, is expected to be completed by the end of February 1997.
Laidlaw is offering C$1.12 billion to acquire all AMR shares and would assume about C$60 million of AMR debt.
With cash proceeds of about C$1.2 billion received in December 1996 from the sale of its solid waste business, Laidlaw has sufficient funds on hand for the AMR acquisition, DBRS said.

The bond rating service said Laidlaw is paying full price for AMR (about 10 times AMR's 1996 estimated EBITDA or seven times 1997 forecast EBITDA, which includes C$20 million of operating cost savings from the merger.) The deal also includes about C$770 million of goodwill, DBRS said.

It said the overall impact of the acquisition is seen as essentially benign for Laidlaw's balance sheet, as gross debt holds in the range of 45 percent of capitalization and proceeds from one divestiture fund a new acquisition.
Longer term, the shift of operations out of slow growth waste management and into the health transportation business should be positive for earnings growth, DBRS said.

Laidlaw also agreed to sell its hazardous waste business to Rollins for C$400 million in cash, a C$350 million convertible debenture and 120 million common shares of the new merged firm, to be called Laidlaw Environmental Services Inc.
But Laidlaw anticipates annual cost savings of C$70 million following the merger and subsequent rationalization of the hazardous waste operations.
DBRS said the merger also removes a weak competitor from the industry and in the longer term should provide for better pricing discipline and profitability for the industry.

Overall, the two deals should be favorable, as Laidlaw expands its core transportation operations through the AMR takeover, while the Rollins deal gives the company greater flexibility should it decide to divest its remaining operations in the waste management business, DBRS said.
